column2: Alone among the books on this shelf, this one has no hand-typed transcription behind it: the text was read off the printed page by machine, and machines misread. We have set the chapters, rejoined the words the printer broke across a line, and cleared away the running heads and page numbers the scanner mistook for text. If you find a word that reads oddly, it is worth reporting — see the note at the front.
column3:
No hand-typed transcription stands behind this book. Its text was read off the printed page by machine, then read a second time by another, and wherever the two readings differed the 1918 page itself decided. Lines the first reading lost are restored, misread words are corrected, and the footnotes it ran into the text are set as notes again. The page numbers in Pink’s own notes are those of the 1918 printing.

\n

The words broken across a line are rejoined, and the running heads and page numbers are cleared away. The printer’s few slips are corrected (futhermore is furthermore); Pink’s own spellings, and the King James words he quotes, stand.
